dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Rosa. How can I help you?
Hello? [pause] Hello? Oh. Hm. I think it hung up on me.
Hello, is anybody there? I pressed the number and there was a long quiet and then I thought, well, that's it, they hung up.
No, I'm here, ma'am. There's a little pause on our recording before it connects to a person. Sorry about that. What can I do for you?
Okay. So it was not a hangup. I should have waited. [pause] I am calling about a dog. Um. Is this the right place for a dog?
Animal control complaints, yes, I can take that down or point you the right way. What's going on with the dog?
It is my neighbor's dog. It keeps getting loose. Every few days now. It is out in the yard, and then it is out in the street, and, um. [pause] I am sorry, I lost what I was going to say.
That's okay, take your time. The neighbor's dog keeps getting out.
Yes. Keeps getting out. Thank you. I don't know how, maybe the gate does not latch, or somebody leaves the door open. I do not know. I am only the renter here, I do not want any trouble with anybody.
Understood. Can you describe the dog for me? Size, color, anything like that.

Yes. It is a big dog. Big like a, um, a shepherd, but not quite. Maybe sixty, seventy pounds. It is brown, a kind of dark brown, with a black face. And one ear goes up and one ear goes down. [pause] That is the one I always know it by, the ear.
Okay, big, dark brown, black face, one ear up and one down. Does it wear a collar?
A collar, yes, a red one I think. Red or maybe orange. I do not go close. It does not bite, I do not think, but it runs at you. It runs and jumps. And I am not so quick on my feet anymore, so.
Sure. Has it actually bitten or snapped at anyone that you've seen?

No, no. Not bitten. It barks a lot, loud. It came at me on Tuesday when I was taking out the trash, and I dropped the bag. [pause] The bag broke. Then the dog was in the trash. That was a mess, and I cleaned it, not the neighbor.
That's irritating, I'm sorry. And it's out again today?
This morning, yes. It is raining so hard today and the dog is out in it, running up and down. Soaking wet. I looked out the window at, um, eight maybe. And it was in the road. A car had to stop.
Okay. That's a safety concern with the rain and the traffic. Do you know the neighbor's name or which house it comes from?
I know the house, it is the one next door, the gray one. The name, no. I never learned it. They keep to themselves. [pause] I would rather not say my own address, if that is okay. Do you need it?

For a report, the officer would need the location of the dog's home, so I'd want the street the dog gets loose on. If you're not comfortable giving it, I can give you the animal control number to call directly and you can decide there.
Yes, that is better. I would like that. I just want somebody to tell them to fix the gate. That is all. I am tired of it. Every few days, it is the same.
Alright. I'll give you the animal control line. Do you have something to write with?
One moment. [pause] I have a pen. But no paper. Hm. I will write on my hand, it is fine. Go ahead.

It's the Newport Police Department's non-emergency line, they handle animal control. You can look it up under the city website too, under Police, Animal Control. If the dog is in the road right now and it's dangerous, call them this morning rather than waiting.
Oh. It is the police. I thought it would be, I do not know, a different office. But all right. The non-emergency, not nine-one-one.
Right, not 911 unless someone's being attacked or it's an emergency. Just ask for animal control and describe the dog like you did for me. The ear, the red collar, the size.
The ear. The black face. Big and brown. I will say that. [pause] And what do they do? Do they take the dog away?
Usually an officer goes out, talks to the owner, and can issue a warning or a citation if the dog keeps getting loose. I can't tell you exactly what they'll do in your case.
A warning. That would be fine. I do not want the dog hurt. It is a nice dog, really, just, um, loud. It is the owner I am annoyed at. Not the dog.
That's fair. Do you want me to note on our end that you called, in case anyone follows up? I'd just need a callback number.
Yes, you can write it. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-eight.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-eight. Got it. And it's Anabela?
Anabela Tavares. T-A-V-A-R-E-S. Like the, um. [pause] Sorry. Like it sounds. Yes.
Tavares, got it. I'll put a note that you called about a loose brown dog, repeated problem. The real report will still have to go through the police line though.
Yes, I understand. I will call them. After this. When I finish writing, I mean. [pause] Is it a long wait on that line?
I can't say, it depends on the morning. With the rain it might be busy. If you get a recording, just wait through it. Don't hang up on the pause like before.
Ha. Yes. The pause. I will wait this time. Okay. Thank you, Rosa. That is the name?
That's right, Rosa. Stay dry, ma'am, and keep your distance from that dog.
I will. Thank you. Goodbye.
